rows.basis: Growth in gross 'Computer, network, machinery and equipment': 12,844m − 9,508m = 3,336m. This counts all server and network growth, not only AI, and predates the AI contract wave; it excludes buildings, land and construction in progress.

Growth in gross 'Computer, network, machinery and equipment': 17,258m − 12,844m = 4,414m. This counts all server and network growth, not only AI; it excludes buildings, land and construction in progress.

Growth in gross 'Computer, network, machinery and equipment': 20,989m − 17,258m = 3,731m. This counts all server and network growth, not only AI. The FY2024 release cites Gen2 AI infrastructure demand exceeding supply, in words only.

Growth in gross 'Computer, network, machinery and equipment': 30,345m − 20,989m = 9,356m. This counts all server and network growth, not only AI. Construction in progress rose 10.9bn to 16.5bn (the shell, mixed) and is excluded.

Growth in gross 'Computer, network, machinery and equipment': 59,634m − 30,345m = 29,289m. This counts all server and network growth, not only AI. It excludes construction in progress (up 23.5bn to 40.0bn) and buildings, and excludes customer-supplied GPUs (part of the 75bn prepaid and customer-supplied hardware), which are the customers' spend. The release ties the capital program to AI cloud infrastructure in words only.
Finance lease liabilities at May 31 2025, which the thesis treats as part of Oracle's AI data-center buildout outside cash capex. The note does not separate AI from other leased assets.

Finance lease liabilities of 7,701m at May 31 2026, part of the data-center buildout outside cash capex; the note does not separate AI. It excludes the forward signals: the 260bn of operating leases not yet commenced (15 to 19 year terms) and the 13.3bn plus 19.0bn of purchase obligations, which are not in the pack's facts.

The release says the large increases in RPO and revenue are driven by demand for cloud infrastructure for AI training and inferencing; it gives no amount. Cloud infrastructure was 53% of cloud revenue and RPO was 638bn, but neither is an AI line; no segment is summed.
The May 2024 release expected strong AI demand to push sales and RPO higher and produce double-digit revenue growth in FY2025; it gives no AI amount.
The February 2026 release says market dynamics (AI demand) let Oracle meet and likely exceed its FY27 revenue growth forecast; it gives no AI amount or share.
